source: Garage turbo kits for engines that have no turbo (owner on PR #5, 2026-10-15: 'Turbos cannot be fitted yet to many engines'). One rule, no per-engine files: rg::size_turbo_kit (core/src/turbo_kit.cpp) sizes each kit from the engine's own swept volume and limiter rpm and scales the anchor turbo at constant tip speed, the hardware-family method of physics_sim docs/data_formats/turbo.md. The conversion (boost grid, compression ratio ceiling) is physics_sim docs/data_formats/engine.md 'Adding or removing forced induction'.
anchor_exducer_source: GTX3582R Gen II class compressor wheel 66/82 mm (the anchor file's rotor_inertia_source); only used for the card text.

sizing.volumetric_efficiency_source: [AS] a street engine near its power peak; the demand is an upper estimate at the limiter.
sizing.flow_margin_source: [AS] compressor max flow 40 % above the engine's peak need: room before choke at the limiter without the lag of a much larger wheel.
sizing.efficiency_log_slope_source: [AS] efficiency = anchor 0.80 + 0.127 ln(s): a wheel half the anchor's size reaches ~0.71 (small passenger-car turbos peak at 0.70-0.75), clamped to [efficiency_min, anchor].
sizing.wastegate_to_throat_source: physics_sim turbo templates: wastegate port 3.0 x the turbine throat (a single on a small engine; the anchor's twin uses 2.36).

conversion.max_compression_ratio_source: physics_sim engine.md: a converted engine keeps the compression ratio at or below 10.5 (check_buildable's forced-induction ceiling); 10.0 leaves knock margin on E5 [AS]. Engines below it keep theirs.

boost_control.source: physics_sim turbo configuration templates (gains per unit of target_boost_bar).

masses.source: [AS] part masses of a kit for the car's part-mass tree (rg/part_mass.h, under the engine): estimated, not cited. They are added to the drive's chassis mass with the kit.
masses.turbo_anchor_source: [AS] a GTX3582R-class turbo (the anchor) with compressor and turbine housings, about 10-12 kg (recalled).
masses.turbo_scale_exponent_source: [AS] mass x scale^2 rather than ^3: housings, flanges and the bearing cartridge do not shrink with the wheel the way a solid body would; a half-size wheel gives ~2.8 kg, so turbo_min_kg holds small units at a plausible 5 kg.
masses.manifold_source: [AS] per turbo: a cast or tubular exhaust manifold, downpipe, external or internal wastegate, oil feed/drain and water lines, 6-10 kg (recalled).
masses.intercooler_source: [AS] a front-mount air-to-air intercooler with its charge pipes, couplers and blow-off valve, 8-12 kg (recalled).
masses.intercooler_per_extra_source: [AS] a twin's second compressor needs its own inlet pipe and a Y-pipe into the shared intercooler, about 2 kg.
